boundaries.evidence: The Definition is formulated for an arbitrary separated finite-type complex variety and an arbitrary algebraic action; for the empty variety the nerve, the simplicial sheaf category and the three defining clauses are vacuous, and no clause requires a nonzero object to exist.

The zero complex satisfies all three clauses of the Definition: it is bounded, has Cartesian cohomology and has zero constructible degree-zero restriction, so it is the zero object of the defined category.

For X=pt and a nontrivial group, the action is trivial but the nerve has Z_p=G^p and is not constant. The category retains equivariant Ext; the companion example proves Ext_G^2(k,k)=k for G=C^*. Only a trivial group gives the ordinary point category.

The Definition also covers the degenerate group case of the empty product of general linear groups (the trivial group): then each Z_p is X, Cartesian cohomology is a condition on a constant simplicial sheaf, and the category is the ordinary bounded constructible category.

citations.quote: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models and $B$ in the stated constructible subcategory on the base, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $k$ be a field. Inverse image of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) is exact and $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, where $Rf_*$ is computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements ([[lem-bounded-below-complexes-admit-injective-replacements]], [[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]). For bounded complexes $A,B$ ([[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]) the derived tensor over $k$ is their signed total tensor ([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]), and for bounded $A$ and bounded-below $B$ the derived internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom(A,B)$ is computed by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I_B)$ in a $k$-linear bounded-below injective model $B\to I_B$ ([[def-sheaf-hom]], [[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]). Flasque $k$-sheaves ([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) are acyclic for sections on every open set ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The tensor-Hom adjunction and the dg associativity, evaluation and symmetry identities are natural. No bounded-constructibility claim for the internal Hom is made here; that requires the local geometric supplier of the later constructible items.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space
$(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$
([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally
small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and
iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific
injective resolution
([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are
bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

The canonical pair is a t-structure on $D(\mathcal A)$ and on each of $D^-,D^+,D^b$ by intersection. More generally if $H^i(X)=0$ for $i>a$ and $H^j(Y)=0$ for $j<b$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[n])=0$ for $n<b-a$, and naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[b-a])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(H^aX,H^bY)$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

For a cochain complex $X$, define the **canonical truncations** by

$$ (\tau^{\leq n}X)^i=\begin{cases}X^i&i<n,\\\ker d_X^n&i=n,\\0&i>n,\end{cases}\qquad (\tau^{\geq n}X)^i=\begin{cases}0&i<n,\\\operatorname{coker}d_X^{n-1}&i=n,\\X^i&i>n.\end{cases} $$

The differential into $\ker d_X^n$ is the factorization of $d_X^{n-1}$; the differential out of $\operatorname{coker}d_X^{n-1}$ is induced by $d_X^n$. All other retained differentials are those of $X$. There are natural maps $\tau^{\leq n}X\to X\to\tau^{\geq n}X$. Unlike [[def-brutal-truncation-of-a-complex]], these constructions correct the boundary using the cycle and boundary objects of [[def-cohomology-object-of-a-cochain-complex]].

Every short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow iB\xrightarrow qC\to0$ of cochain complexes gives a natural distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$. In particular, for every integer $n$ there are canonical distinguished triangles

$$\tau^{\leq n}X\to X\to\tau^{\geq n+1}X\to(\tau^{\leq n}X)[1],$$

$$\tau^{\leq n}X\to\tau^{\leq n+1}X\to H^{n+1}(X)[-n-1]\to(\tau^{\leq n}X)[1],$$

$$H^n(X)[-n]\to\tau^{\geq n}X\to\tau^{\geq n+1}X\to H^n(X)[-n+1].$$

The derived category, with shift $[1]$ and distinguished triangles the isomorphic images of cone triangles, is triangulated. The localization functor $Q$ is exact. Every such triangle gives a long exact cohomology sequence $\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(Y)\to H^n(Z)\to H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$.

In $D(\mathcal A)$ let distinguished triangles mean triangles isomorphic to images of cone triangles in $K(\mathcal A)$. The cochain shift descends and these triangles satisfy TR1, signed TR2, and TR3.

Let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of sets on a
topological space $X$. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism if and only if, for
every $x\in X$, the induced map on stalks
$$\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\longrightarrow\mathcal G_x$$
is a bijection.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For complexes of vector spaces over a field $k$ with finite diagonals, cross product is a natural isomorphism $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H_pC\otimes_kH_qD\cong H_n(C\otimes_kD)$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf on $Y$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf on $X$. Then there is a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(f^{-1}\mathcal G,\mathcal F) \cong \operatorname{Hom}_Y(\mathcal G,f_*\mathcal F).$$

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf on $Y$.
The **inverse-image presheaf**
$$
f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G
$$
on $X$ is defined by
$$
(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U):=\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V),
$$
where $V$ runs over the open neighbourhoods of $f(U)$ in $Y$, ordered by
reverse inclusion. If $U' \subseteq U$, then every neighbourhood of $f(U)$ is a
neighbourhood of $f(U')$, so there is a natural restriction map
$(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)\to(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U')$.

The **inverse image sheaf** of a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ is the sheafification
of this presheaf:
$$
f^{-1}\mathcal G:=a(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G).
$$

When $U$ is open in $X$ and $V$ is an open set of $Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$,
there is a canonical map
$$
\mathcal G(V)\longrightarrow(f_{\mathrm p}\mathcal G)(U)
$$
into the colimit class represented by $V$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf on $X$.
The **direct image presheaf**
$$f_*\mathcal F$$
on $Y$ is defined on an open set $V \subseteq Y$ by
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V):=\mathcal F(f^{-1}(V)).
$$
If $V' \subseteq V$, the restriction map
$$
(f_*\mathcal F)(V)\longrightarrow(f_*\mathcal F)(V')
$$
is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ for the inclusion
$f^{-1}(V') \subseteq f^{-1}(V)$.

Thus direct image is just precomposition of the presheaf with the inverse-image
map on open sets.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The local comparison and the fiber model.** Let $V\subseteq S$ be a product chart with trivialization $Y|_V\cong V\times F$ and projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$. By [F1] there is a natural comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B_V\simeq B_V\otimes_kC^*(F;k)$ for bounded $B_V\in D_c^b(V;k)$, compatible with restriction to smaller charts and carrying the adjunction unit to $B_V\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. By [F2] the chart and the fiber carry finite deleted-boundary models, so $C^*(F;k)$ is a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces whose cohomology is $k$ in degree zero, in the sense that the structure map $k\to C^*(F;k)$ identifies $k$ with $H^0$, and is zero in degrees $1\le j\le r$. The comparison is compatible with the global adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [F3] over the chart: restriction to $V$ is inverse image along the open inclusion, inverse image commutes with $f^*$, $Rf_*$ commutes with restriction to the open base for open inclusions by [F3] and [F8], and the unit is natural, so the restriction of the global unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ to $V$ is the chart unit.

**The cone bound.** Let $\tilde C:=\operatorname{Cone}(k\to C^*(F;k))$, a bounded complex of finite-dimensional vector spaces with $H^0(\tilde C)=0$ and $H^j(\tilde C)=H^j(C^*(F;k))=0$ for $1\le j\le r$; hence $H^j(\tilde C)=0$ for all $j\le r$. Now let $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$, so $H^p(B)=0$ for $p<b$. By [F7] the cohomology of $B_V\otimes_k\tilde C$ is the direct sum of the terms $H^p(B_V)\otimes_kH^q(\tilde C)$ with $p+q=n$, and a nonzero such term needs $p\ge b$ and $q\ge r+1$, hence $n\ge b+r+1$; therefore $H^n(B_V\otimes_k\tilde C)=0$ for $n\le b+r$. Since the unit of the chart comparison is $B_V\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$, its cone is $B_V\otimes_k\tilde C$ up to canonical isomorphism, so the cone of the chart unit lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$ on every chart. The charts cover $S$, the restriction of the global unit to each chart is the chart unit by step 1.1, and vanishing of the cohomology sheaves of a complex is a local condition [F6], so the cone of the global unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}$, which proves claim 1.

**The Hom comparison.** Let $B\to Rf_*f^*B\to C\to B[1]$ be the distinguished triangle of the unit, with $C\in D^{\ge b+r+1}$ by step 2.1, and let $A\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$ and $m\le b+r-a$. By [F5], $C[m]\in D^{\ge b+r+1-m}$ and $C[m-1]\in D^{\ge b+r+2-m}$; since $m\le b+r-a$ gives $b+r+1-m>a$ and $b+r+2-m>a$, orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le a},D^{\ge a+1})=0$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m])=0=\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m-1])$. The long exact Hom sequence of [F4] applied to the triangle, shifted by $[m]$, therefore shows that the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*f^*B[m])$ is a bijection. Under the derived adjunction of [F3] this map corresponds to the composition with the unit, $u\mapsto\eta_{B[m]}\circ u$, whose adjoint is exactly pullback $u\mapsto f^*u$; since the adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,Rf_*f^*B[m])$ carries $f^*u$ to $\eta_{B[m]}\circ u$ by naturality of the unit, the induced pullback map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ is a bijection. This proves claim 2.

**The image criterion.** Assume $a-b\le r$ and put $\Phi=f^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ and $\Psi=\tau^{\le a}\circ Rf_*$. For $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r+1}\subseteq D^{\ge a+1}$ by step 2.1 and $b+r+1>a$, so the truncated unit $B\to\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B$ is an isomorphism; its inverse gives $\Psi\Phi\cong\operatorname{id}$. Now let $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$. Since $C\in D^{\ge b}$ and $Rf_*$ preserves lower bounds (a bounded-below complex can be resolved in degrees at least $b$ by [F4], and $f_*$ of a complex vanishing below $b$ vanishes below $b$), we get $Rf_*C\in D^{\ge b}(S;k)$, and by the setting $Rf_*C$ has bounded constructible cohomology; hence $\Psi C=\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Let $\gamma_C:\Phi\Psi C\to C$ be the composite of $\Phi(\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to Rf_*C)$ with the counit $\varepsilon_C:\Phi Rf_*C\to C$ of the adjunction. If $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism, then $C\cong\Phi(\Psi C)$ with $\Psi C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$, so $C$ lies in the image of $\Phi$. Conversely, let $C=\Phi B=f^*B$ with $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Then $\Psi C=\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B$, and the truncation $\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B\to Rf_*f^*B$ factors, up to the canonical isomorphism $\tau^{\le a}Rf_*f^*B\cong B$ supplied by the previous paragraph, as the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$; the triangle identity $\varepsilon_{f^*B}\circ f^*(\eta_B)=\operatorname{id}_{f^*B}$, together with exactness of $f^*$, therefore shows that $\gamma_{f^*B}$ is an isomorphism. Hence for $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ the counit $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism exactly when $C$ is a pullback, which is the first assertion of claim 4.

**Full faithfulness.** If $a-b\le r$, then $0\le b+r-a$, so claim 2 with $m=0$ gives that $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B)$ is a bijection for all objects $A,B$ of $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Inverse image is exact and preserves the canonical t-structure and algebraic constructibility by [F3] and [F6], so $f^*$ maps $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$ into $D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$; a functor between categories that is bijective on all Hom sets is fully faithful, so claim 3 follows.

**Retracts.** Let $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ be a direct summand of $\Phi B=f^*B$ for some $B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$, with maps $i:C\to\Phi B$ and $p:\Phi B\to C$ satisfying $pi=\operatorname{id}_C$. The counit $\gamma$ is a natural transformation $\Phi\Psi\to\operatorname{id}$; naturality in the form $u\circ\gamma_X=\gamma_Y\circ\Phi\Psi(u)$ for $u:X\to Y$, applied to $u=i$ and $u=p$, gives $p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\Phi\Psi(i)=p\circ i\circ\gamma_C=\gamma_C$ and $\gamma_C\circ\Phi\Psi(p)=p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}$. By step 3.2 the map $\gamma_{\Phi B}$ is an isomorphism. Define $\delta:=\Phi\Psi(p)\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ i:C\to\Phi\Psi C$. Then $\delta\circ\gamma_C=\Phi\Psi(p)\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\Phi\Psi(i)=\Phi\Psi(pi)=\operatorname{id}_{\Phi\Psi C}$ and $\gamma_C\circ\delta=p\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}\circ\gamma_{\Phi B}^{-1}\circ i=pi=\operatorname{id}_C$, using the two displayed identities. Hence $\gamma_C$ is an isomorphism and, by step 3.2, $C$ lies in the image of $\Phi$, which proves closure under direct summands.

**Extensions under the strict bound.** Assume $r\ge a-b+1$ and let $C'\to C\to C''\to C'[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ whose outer objects lie in the image: $C'=f^*B'$ and $C''=f^*B''$ with $B',B''\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Let $\varphi:C''\to C'[1]$ be its connecting morphism. Because $1\le b+r-a$ by the strict bound, claim 2 applies with $A=B''\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$, $B=B'\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ and $m=1$; the isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(B'',B'[1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*B'',f^*B'[1])$ being pullback along $f^*$, there is a unique $\bar\varphi:B''\to B'[1]$ with $f^*\bar\varphi=\varphi$. By TR1 the morphism $\bar\varphi$ is completed to a distinguished triangle $B'\to\bar B\to B''\to B'[1]$ in $D^b(S;k)$ ([F5]). The long exact cohomology sequence of this triangle and $B',B''\in D^{[b,a]}$ show $H^j(\bar B)=0$ for $j<b$ and for $j>a$: the exact segment $H^j(B')\to H^j(\bar B)\to H^j(B'')$ has zero outer terms in both ranges. By [F6] the cone $\bar B$ of a morphism of bounded algebraically constructible complexes is bounded and algebraically constructible, so $\bar B\in D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$. Exactness of $f^*$ [F3] turns the triangle on $\bar\varphi$ into a distinguished triangle with connecting morphism $f^*\bar\varphi=\varphi$; two distinguished triangles with the same connecting morphism are isomorphic on their third objects, because TR2 and TR3 applied to the identity on the source and target of the connecting morphism give a morphism between the two triangles whose first two components are identities and hence, by the five-lemma applied to the long exact Hom sequences of [F4], an isomorphism on the third objects. Thus $C\cong f^*\bar B$ lies in the image of $\Phi$. This proves the extension-closure clause of claim 4; at the boundary $r=a-b$ the degree-one comparison $1\le b+r-a$ fails and the argument is deliberately not used.

**Conclusion and the local nature of the comparison.** Step 2.1 proves the cone claim 1; step 3.1 proves the Hom comparison claim 2, step 4.1 full faithfulness claim 3, and steps 3.2, 4.2 and 4.3 the image criterion and the closure properties of claim 4. The comparison used in step 2.1 is the local product comparison on product charts, not a global splitting: no isomorphism $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is asserted, and the argument uses only the cone of the unit and the degreewise vanishing of the fiber model, so nonzero characteristic-class transgressions of the bundle are preserved. The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and

It is obtained recursively from

$$u_k=v_k-\sum_{j<k}\langle v_k,e_j\rangle e_j,\qquad e_k=\frac{u_k}{\lVert u_k\rVert}.$$

  component** of $x$ is its equivalence class

When $F$ is nonempty the charts imply surjectivity by taking one point in the chart fiber for each particular base point; this assertion does not require choosing a simultaneous section. Over a point a chart identifies $E$ with $F$. No AC is assumed in the definition.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The frame retraction.** Fix $n\le N$ and let $A\in\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ have columns $v_0,\dots,v_{n-1}$, a linearly independent list. Applying the Gram-Schmidt recursion of [F1] to $(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ gives an orthonormal list $(e_0,\dots,e_{n-1})$ with $\operatorname{span}(e_0,\dots,e_{k-1})=\operatorname{span}(v_0,\dots,v_{k-1})$ for every $k$, so the upper triangular matrix $R$ with $R_{jk}=\langle v_k,e_j\rangle$ for $j<k$, $R_{kk}=\lVert u_k\rVert>0$ and $R_{jk}=0$ for $j>k$ satisfies $A=QR$ with $Q=(e_0,\dots,e_{n-1})\in V_n(\mathbb C^N)$. The Gram-Schmidt formulas are continuous rational expressions with positive denominators on the full-rank locus, so $A\mapsto(Q(A),R(A))$ is continuous. Writing $R=DU$ with $D$ the diagonal part and $U$ unit upper triangular, the family $t\mapsto Q(A)\bigl((1-t)D+tI\bigr)\bigl((1-t)U+tI\bigr)$ is continuous, has invertible upper triangular second factor with positive diagonal for every $t\in[0,1]$, and connects $A$ to $Q(A)$ inside $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$; at $t=1$ it is $Q(A)$, so $A\mapsto Q(A)$ is a deformation retraction onto $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$. This proves claim 1 and shows that $U_N$ is homotopy equivalent to $\prod_iV_{n_i}(\mathbb C^{N_i})$.

**Compact smooth frame manifolds.** Let $f(A)=A^*A$ from the open full-rank locus of $\mathbb C^{N\times n}$ to the real vector space $\operatorname{Herm}(n)$. Its differential is $H\mapsto A^*H+H^*A$; for Hermitian $B$, taking $H=\tfrac12A(A^*A)^{-1}B$ gives $A^*H=H^*A=B/2$, hence differential $B$. Thus $I_n$ is a regular value and $V_n=f^{-1}(I_n)$ is a smooth submanifold by [F2]. It is closed in the ambient Euclidean space and bounded, since each frame column has norm one, so it is compact by [F3]. The subspace is Hausdorff and second countable, as required by the triangulation supplier. For $n=0$ it is a point.

**The forgetting bundle.** Fix $w\in V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ and an orthonormal basis $c_1,\ldots,c_{N-n+1}$ of its orthogonal complement. For a nearby frame $w'$, put $P_{w'}=I-w'w'^*$. The vectors $P_{w'}c_j$ remain linearly independent near $w$, since their Gram determinant is continuous and equals one at $w$. Gram-Schmidt gives a continuously varying orthonormal basis $c_j(w')$ of the complement of $w'$. The map $(w',z)\mapsto(w',\sum_jz_jc_j(w'))$ for $z\in S^{2(N-n)+1}\subset\mathbb C^{N-n+1}$ trivializes the forgetting map; its continuous inverse takes the inner products with $c_j(w')$. This also covers $n=1$ over the point $V_0$. By step 1.2 the base is compact Hausdorff, so [F4] supplies a finite subordinate partition of unity and makes the bundle numerable, hence Hurewicz and Serre.

**Finite CW model and path-connectedness.** By the triangulation theorem of [F3] applied to the compact smooth manifold $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$, there is a finite simplicial complex $K_n$ and a homeomorphism $|K_n|\to V_n(\mathbb C^N)$. A finite simplicial complex is a finite CW complex: its cells are the open simplices, the characteristic maps are the inclusions of the closed simplices, closure finiteness holds because there are finitely many simplices, and the weak topology agrees with the topology of the realization because the realization is the finite union of its closed simplices. Hence $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, as claimed in claim 2. For path-connectedness, induct on $n$. The space $V_0(\mathbb C^N)$ is a point. For $n\ge1$ the map $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ is the locally trivial bundle of step 2.1 with fiber the nonempty path-connected sphere $S^{2(N-n)+1}$ by [F6], and the base is path-connected by the induction hypothesis; the local connectedness argument of [F8] then makes $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ path-connected. This completes claim 2.

**The gap for one factor.** Induct on $n$, starting with $V_0$ a point. For $n\ge1$ put $d=2(N-n)+1$. The forgetting bundle of step 2.1 has fibre $S^d$ and base homeomorphic to a path-connected finite CW complex by step 3.1. The induction hypothesis gives vanishing of the base cohomology in degrees $1$ through $2(N-n+1)=d+1$. In the Serre spectral sequence [F5], [F6] makes all fibre rows in degrees $1,\ldots,d-1$ zero; the degree-zero coefficient system is constant $k$, since the fibre is connected. Consequently all $E_2$ terms of total degree $1,\ldots,d-1$ are zero, while $E_2^{0,0}=k$. No differential can enter $(0,0)$ or leave it in this first-quadrant sequence. Strong convergence therefore gives $H^0(V_n;k)=k$ and $H^j(V_n;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le d-1=2(N-n)$, completing the induction. No constancy of the top-degree fibre coefficient system is needed.

**The product.** By step 1.1 it suffices to compute the cohomology of $\prod_{i=1}^sV_{n_i}(\mathbb C^{N_i})$, and we induct on $s$. For $s=1$ this is step 4.1. For $s\ge2$ let $P=\prod_{i<s}V_{n_i}(\mathbb C^{N_i})$ and consider the projection $P\times V_{n_s}(\mathbb C^{N_s})\to P$, a trivial bundle with fiber $V_{n_s}(\mathbb C^{N_s})$, hence numerable and a Serre fibration by [F4]. By step 3.1 each factor and, inductively, $P$ is homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and a finite product of finite CW complexes is again a finite CW complex: identify $D^a\times D^b$ with $D^{a+b}$ by radial rescaling between their unit balls; the product characteristic maps into the product space then give cells $e\times e'$ and a finite cell decomposition, closure finiteness holds because there are finitely many cells, and the weak topology of the product cell structure agrees with the product topology for finite compact Hausdorff complexes, where the compactly generated product topology coincides with the ordinary one. So [F5] applies to the projection with constant coefficient system in fiber degree $0$. If $H^0(P;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(P;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_{s-1}=\min_{i<s}2(N_i-n_i)$ by induction, and if $H^0(V_{n_s};k)\cong k$, $H^j(V_{n_s};k)=0$ for $1\le j\le2(N_{s}-n_s)$ by step 4.1, then in total degree $m\le r_s=\min(r_{s-1},2(N_s-n_s))$ every nonzero $E_2^{a,b}$ with $a+b=m$ has $b=0$, for $b\ge1$ would need fiber cohomology in degree $b\le r_s\le2(N_s-n_s)$, which vanishes; the differential bookkeeping of step 4.1 then gives $H^m(P\times V_{n_s};k)\cong H^m(P;k)$, which is $k$ for $m=0$ and $0$ for $1\le m\le r_s$. This proves claim 3, $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$, by the homotopy equivalence of step 1.1.

**The cohomology convention.** The full-rank spaces are Euclidean open subsets and the Stiefel spaces and their products are smooth metric manifolds with contractible-open chart bases. Thus [F7] identifies their constant-sheaf cohomology with the singular cohomology computed in steps 4.1 and 5.1; naturality carries the frame deformation retraction of step 1.1 to these comparisons. In particular the same gap holds for the constant-sheaf fibre cohomology used by the later derived pullback lemmas.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 5.1 give claims 1 and 3; steps 1.2, 2.1 and 3.1 give claim 2. AC is consumed only through the named compactness, triangulation, partition-of-unity, spectral-sequence and constant-sheaf comparison suppliers [F3]-[F7], as recorded in [A1].

citations.quote:
Let $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $0\leq n\leq N$.
The **Stiefel space**

$$V_n(\mathbb F^N)=\{(v_1,\ldots,v_n):\langle v_i,v_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\}$$

has the subspace topology from $(\mathbb F^N)^n$. The group
$K_n=\operatorname O(n)$ in the real case and
$K_n=\operatorname U(n)$ in the complex case acts freely on the right by
change of orthonormal frame. The **Grassmannian**
$\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)=V_n(\mathbb F^N)/K_n$ is the space of
$n$-planes with this quotient topology.

Graph charts about a plane identify nearby planes with linear maps to its
orthogonal complement. They locally trivialize
$V_n(\mathbb F^N)\to\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)$ as a principal
$K_n$-bundle. Its associated standard vector bundle, in the convention of
[[def-frame-bundle-and-associated-vector-bundle]], is the **tautological
bundle**

$$\gamma_n^N=\{(W,v)\in\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N)\times\mathbb F^N:v\in W\}.$$

Equivalently, its graph-chart transition matrices glue it by
[[thm-vector-bundles-glued-from-transition-cocycles]].

The coordinate inclusions $\mathbb F^N\subseteq\mathbb F^{N+1}$ define
compatible inclusions of Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and tautological
bundles. Write

$$V_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}V_n(\mathbb F^N),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^\infty)=\bigcup_{N\geq n}\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb F^N),$$

with the weak direct-limit topology: a set is closed exactly when its
intersection with every finite stage is closed. The later Schubert theorem
identifies this with the weak topology in
[[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]. For $n=0$,
the Stiefel spaces, Grassmannians, and their stable colimits are points, and
$\gamma_0$ is the zero bundle.

A left action of a group $G$ on a set $X$ ([[def-group-action]]) is **free**
when

$$g\cdot x=x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g=e$$

for every $g\in G$ and $x\in X$. Equivalently, no nonidentity element of $G$
fixes any point of $X$.

Let $G$ be a topological group, as in [[def-topological-group]], with identity $1$. A **right principal $G$-bundle** is a continuous map $\pi:P\to B$ with a continuous right action $(p,g)\mapsto pg$, satisfying $p1=p$, $(pg)h=p(gh)$ and $\pi(pg)=\pi(p)$, together with equivariant bundle charts $\theta_i:\pi^{-1}(U_i)\cong U_i\times G$ over an open cover. Equivariance means $\theta_i(pg)=(b,ag)$ whenever $\theta_i(p)=(b,a)$. Charts use ordinary products as in [[def-locally-trivial-fiber-bundle]]. In each fiber the action is free and transitive: right multiplication on $G$ has those properties and the chart identifies the actions. Freeness alone is not the definition.

A **left $G$-space** is a topological space $F$ with a continuous map $(g,x)\mapsto gx$ such that $1x=x$ and $g(hx)=(gh)x$. Effectiveness of this action is not required. Define
$$P\times_G F=(P\times F)/\bigl((pg,x)\sim(p,gx)\bigr)$$
with the ordinary quotient topology, and write $[p,x]$ for its points. Precisely, the relation is the orbit relation of the right action $(p,x)\cdot g=(pg,g^{-1}x)$. Its action law is $((p,x)\cdot g)\cdot h=(pgh,h^{-1}g^{-1}x)=(p,x)\cdot(gh)$, and its generating relations are exactly the displayed ones. Thus the equivalence relation and quotient are defined without choosing orbit representatives.

The projection $r([p,x])=\pi(p)$ is well-defined and continuous by [[thm-quotient-universal-property]], since $(p,x)\mapsto\pi(p)$ is continuous and constant on every orbit. This is the **associated fiber-bundle construction**; the next proposition proves its local triviality and pullback property. The quotient construction and projection already make sense before that proof.

If $B$ is empty then $P$ is empty. If $F$ is empty the associated space is empty even for nonempty $B$; this is allowed by our bundle convention. For singleton $F$ the construction is the orbit projection of the principal bundle. For the trivial group it is the product with $F$ over the chart-identified base. No AC is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $s\ge1$,
$n_i\ge1$ and $N_i\ge n_i+1$ for $1\le i\le s$, let $k$ be a field, and put
$$U_N=\prod_{i=1}^{s}\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad r_N=2\min_{i}(N_i-n_i),$$
where $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is the open set of
injective, equivalently full-rank, complex $N\times n$ matrices. Then:

1. each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to
   the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)=\{A\in\mathbb C^{N\times n}:A^*A=I_n\}$
   of orthonormal frames
   ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]]);
2. each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold and is
   homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the map
   $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ forgetting the last column is a
   numerable locally trivial fiber bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a
   Hurewicz and a Serre fibration;
3. $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.

No claim is made about the cohomology of $U_N$ above degree $r_N$, and no
GL-equivariance of the retractions or trivializations below is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:Y\to S$ be an algebraic map that is a
locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting of
[[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]]
and
[[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]]:
$S$ and $Y$ are the analytic spaces of separated finite-type complex varieties,
$Y$ trivializes over charts $V$ of $S$ carrying the finite conical cochain
models of the second supplier as products $V\times F\to V$, and the nonempty
connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$ carries a finite deleted-boundary model.
Suppose the constant-sheaf cohomology of the fiber is $k$ in degree zero and
vanishes in degrees $1,\dots,r$: $H^0(F;k)=k$ and $H^j(F;k)=0$ for
$1\le j\le r$, computed by the finite model. Finally, in the setting the
pushforward of every bounded algebraically constructible complex considered
below again has bounded algebraically constructible cohomology, with the finite
models supplied by the two named lemmas. Then, for bounded algebraically
constructible complexes of $k$-sheaves:

1. for $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to
   $D^{\ge b+r+1}$;
2. pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ whenever
   $A\in D_c^{\le a}(S;k)$, $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ and $m\le b+r-a$;
3. if $a-b\le r$, then $f^*$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
   $D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)$;
4. if $a-b\le r$, then an object $C\in D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ lies in the image of
   $f^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(S;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(Y;k)$ if and only if the counit
   $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ is an isomorphism; the image is closed under
   direct summands, and it is closed under extensions when the stronger bound
   $r\ge a-b+1$ holds;
5. no global tensor splitting $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is
   asserted: the comparison is local and genuine characteristic-class
   transgressions are preserved.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models and $B$ in the stated constructible subcategory on the base, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by a normalized double complex; before normalization its spectral sequence has first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. For algebraic principal $\mathrm{GL}$ bundles of separated finite-type complex varieties (Zariski locally trivial bundles) this restricts to the algebraically constructible subcategories, with constructibility required at every simplicial level.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize

[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

For a triangulated category $T$ with shift $[1]$, a **t-structure** is a pair of strictly full subcategories $(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq0})$ such that $T^{\leq0}[1]\subseteq T^{\leq0}$, $T^{\geq0}[-1]\subseteq T^{\geq0}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_T(T^{\leq0},T^{\geq1})=0$, and every $X$ has a distinguished triangle $A\to X\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in T^{\leq0}$ and $B\in T^{\geq1}$. Here $T^{\geq1}=T^{\geq0}[-1]$ and $T^{\leq n}=T^{\leq0}[-n]$, $T^{\geq n}=T^{\geq0}[-n]$. Its **heart** is $T^{\leq0}\cap T^{\geq0}$.

For the triangulation of [[thm-the-derived-category-inherits-a-triangulated-structure]], the canonical candidate is $D^{\leq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i>0\}$ and $D^{\geq0}=\{X:H^i(X)=0\text{ for }i<0\}$, using [[prop-cohomology-factors-through-the-derived-category]].

The canonical pair is a t-structure on $D(\mathcal A)$ and on each of $D^-,D^+,D^b$ by intersection. More generally if $H^i(X)=0$ for $i>a$ and $H^j(Y)=0$ for $j<b$, then $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[n])=0$ for $n<b-a$, and naturally $\operatorname{Hom}_D(X,Y[b-a])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(H^aX,H^bY)$.

The derived category, with shift $[1]$ and distinguished triangles the isomorphic images of cone triangles, is triangulated. The localization functor $Q$ is exact. Every such triangle gives a long exact cohomology sequence $\cdots\to H^n(X)\to H^n(Y)\to H^n(Z)\to H^{n+1}(X)\to\cdots$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **The frame bundle and its nerve.** On a Grassmannian chart determined by an invertible $n\times n$ pivot minor, a frame is uniquely $\binom{I_n}{T}h$, with $h\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$ and $T$ the graph coordinates. These formulas and their inverses are regular, so they give algebraic principal-bundle charts for $U_N\to B_N$. In these charts the diagonal quotient is $V\times X$, with $(\binom{I}{T}h,x)$ mapping to $(T,hx)$, and the principal quotient $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ has section $(T,y)\mapsto(\binom{I}{T},y)$. The finitely many charts glue by the regular change-of-frame maps; they exhibit $X_N$ as a separated finite-type variety and $q_N$ as a principal $G$-bundle. Its action nerve is its Čech nerve, so [F5] applies. Projection to $X$ is equivariant for the left action specified in the Statement, and induces the simplicial map $p_N$. In degree $m$ this is a product projection $G^m\times U_N\times X\to G^m\times X$ with fibre $U_N$; its structure squares are Cartesian, since group action on the frame factor is invertible.

**The fiber is $r_N$-acyclic with finite models.** By [F2], $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$, and the product of Stiefel models supplies the bounded finite cochain model of the fiber with coefficient-field compatibility. By [F4] the base $G^m\times X$ carries the finite conical cochain models, so each levelwise projection of step 1.1 is a locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting with $r_N$-acyclic fiber.

**The simplicial unit bound.** For a map of these nerves, the levelwise direct images acquire simplicial structure by the canonical sheaf base-change maps followed by the source structure maps. The levelwise adjunction gives $p_N^*\dashv p_{N*}$, with exact inverse image. Evaluation of a simplicial injective at degree $m$ is injective: evaluation has an exact left adjoint, whose degree-$l$ term is the direct sum over operators $[m]\to[l]$ of their inverse images of the given sheaf. These sums and inverse images are exact. Thus a bounded-below simplicial injective replacement evaluates to an injective replacement at every level, and $(Rp_{N*}C)_m=Rp_{N,m*}C_m$. For $B\ge b$, [F3] and step 2.1 give that the cone of $B_m\to Rp_{N,m*}p_{N,m}^*B_m$ lies in $D^{\ge b+r_N+1}$ at every level. The same bound therefore holds for the simplicial unit cone in the bounded-below derived category; no augmentation of the action nerve to $X$ is used.

**The simplicial Hom comparison.** The simplicial category has the exact levelwise inverse image $p_N^*$ left adjoint to the levelwise direct image $Rp_{N*}$ and carries the canonical t-structure of [F7], whose aisles are defined cohomology-objectwise and hence are the levelwise aisles. With the cone bound of step 3.1 in place, the argument of [F3] — its Hom comparison, image criterion, full faithfulness and its retract and extension clauses — applies verbatim inside the simplicial bounded-below derived category, with its bounded full subcategory: for $A\in D^{\le a}$ and $B\in D^{\ge b}$ the long exact Hom sequence of the unit triangle and the orthogonality $\operatorname{Hom}(D^{\le a},D^{\ge a+1})=0$ identify the pullback map $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m'])\to\operatorname{Hom}(p_N^*A,p_N^*B[m'])$ as an isomorphism for $m'\le b+r_N-a$; for $a-b\le r_N$ it is fully faithful on the full subcategory $D^{[b,a]}$; and on that interval an object lies in the image exactly when the truncated counit $p_N^*\tau^{\le a}Rp_{N*}C\to C$ is an isomorphism, the image being closed under retracts and under extensions when $r_N\ge a-b+1$. Every input of that argument is an input already verified here: the adjunction and levelwise model [F5], the cone bound of step 3.1, and the t-structure orthogonality [F7].

**Descent and the functor $Q_N$.** Restricting the conclusion of step 4.1 to the full subcategory of Cartesian objects identified with $D_c^b(X_N;k)$ by [F5], the functor $p_N^*$ followed by descent is $Q_N$: for $F\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ the object $p_N^*F$ has Cartesian cohomology because $p_N$ is a simplicial map and the structure squares of $p_N^*$ are Cartesian by naturality of inverse image; descent produces $Q_N(F)\in D_c^b(X_N;k)$, and $q_N^*Q_N(F)\cong p_N^*F$ canonically. Hence, for $A\le a$, $B\ge b$ and $m\le b+r_N-a$, the isomorphisms of step 4.1 compose with the descent equivalence to give $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$, proving claim 1; the same composition proves claim 2 on intervals of width at most $r_N$.

**The image and Cartesian descent.** Necessity follows from $q_N^*Q_N(A)=\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_0$ at degree zero. Conversely suppose $H\in D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ and $q_N^*H\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$ for $F\in D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)$. Let $C$ be the Cartesian simplicial pullback of $H$ to the principal-bundle nerve, and put $E=\tau^{\le a}Rp_{N*}C$ in the ambient simplicial category. It lies in $[b,a]$ because derived direct image preserves lower bounds. At every level $m$, Cartesianity identifies $C_m$ with the pullback of $C_0$, hence with $p_{N,m}^*\operatorname{pr}_{X,m}^*F$, where $\operatorname{pr}_{X,m}:G^m\times X\to X$ is projection. The levelwise image criterion [F3] therefore makes the truncated counit $p_N^*E\to C$ an isomorphism in every degree. Its naturality compares the structure maps of $p_N^*E$ with the Cartesian maps of $C$. Each $p_{N,m}$ is surjective and its structure squares are Cartesian, so its exact pullback reflects these quasi-isomorphisms; hence $E$ has Cartesian cohomology. Moreover $E_0\cong F$ by the truncated unit and $C_0\cong\operatorname{pr}_X^*F$, so it is algebraically constructible. Thus $E\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ and Čech descent gives $Q_N(E)\cong H$. Retracts and extensions under $r_N\ge a-b+1$ lift by the degree-zero and degree-one Hom comparisons of step 4.1; their cones and summands have bounded Cartesian constructible cohomology, and the same counit argument gives the image. This proves claim 3 without assuming that ordinary descent data automatically strictify.

**Coherence and the trivial group.** The product $U_N\times U_M$ is a free smooth $G$-resolution in its own right. Its projections to $U_N$ and $U_M$ descend to $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$, locally trivial bundles with fibres $U_M$ and $U_N$. Their pullbacks are fully faithful on the stated intervals by [F3] and the bounds $r_M,r_N$. On the common principal bundle $U_N\times U_M\times X$, both pulled-back representatives have the canonical descent identification with the same pullback of $A$ from $X$; these identifications are compatible with the principal-bundle nerve maps, so [F5]'s descent equivalence yields a canonical isomorphism $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)\simeq\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$. Naturality is inherited from those same inverse-image and descent maps. On the triple product all comparisons identify the representatives with the same pullback of $A$, so their two compositions agree and the cocycle law follows. This compares objects and Hom maps in the common category, without equating the two different target categories or identifying the product with a larger frame space. If $G$ is trivial, take the point as its resolution; then $X_N=X$, the action nerve is constant at $X$, $r_N=\infty$ and $Q_N$ is the identity. This proves claims 4 and 5.

**Conclusion.** Steps 3.1 to 5.1 prove claims 1 and 2, step 6.1 claim 3, and step 7.1 claims 4 and 5. The comparison is used only on the nerve and through the finite local models: no global splitting of $Ra_{N*}a_N^*B$ is asserted, so genuine characteristic-class transgressions are preserved. AC enters only through [A1].

citations.quote: Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by a normalized double complex; before normalization its spectral sequence has first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. For algebraic principal $\mathrm{GL}$ bundles of separated finite-type complex varieties (Zariski locally trivial bundles) this restricts to the algebraically constructible subcategories, with constructibility required at every simplicial level.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field of
characteristic zero, let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic
variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]),
regarded with its analytic topology as in
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]])
acting algebraically on $X$
([[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). Equip the
finite product $G$ with its usual topology and the product $G^p\times X$ with
the product topology.

**The action nerve.** For $p\ge0$ put $Z_p=G^p\times X$, where $G^0$ is a
one-point space, so that $Z_0=X$, and let
$d_i:Z_p\to Z_{p-1}$ for $p\ge1$ $(0\le i\le p)$ and $s_i:Z_p\to Z_{p+1}$ for $p\ge0$
$(0\le i\le p)$ be the face and degeneracy maps of the nerve of the
translation groupoid $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$: writing
$(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)\in Z_p$,
$$d_0(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_2,\ldots,g_p,x),\qquad d_p(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{p-1},g_px),$$
$$d_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_{i-1},g_ig_{i+1},g_{i+2},\ldots,g_p,x)\quad(0<i<p),$$
$$s_i(g_1,\ldots,g_p,x)=(g_1,\ldots,g_i,e,g_{i+1},\ldots,g_p,x).$$
These are continuous and satisfy the simplicial identities, so $Z_\bullet$ is a
simplicial space in the sense of
[[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]]; equivalently, a
simplicial operator $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ acts by a continuous map
$Z_\alpha:Z_m\to Z_p$. In general this action nerve has no augmentation to
$X$: already the two faces $G\times X\rightrightarrows X$ are projection and
action and need not agree. For a free action with principal quotient
$P\to P/G$, its action nerve is instead augmented over $P/G$, as in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Simplicial sheaves.** A simplicial sheaf of $k$-vector spaces on
$Z_\bullet$ is a family $F=(F_p)_{p\ge0}$ in which $F_p$ is a sheaf of
$k$-vector spaces on $Z_p$ ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-module-on-ringed-space]]) together with structure morphisms
$Z_\alpha^{-1}F_p\to F_m$ for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$, subject to
the identity and composition identities; a morphism $F\to G$ is a levelwise
family of $k$-linear sheaf maps commuting with the structure morphisms.
Kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (cokernels after sheafification of
the presheaf cokernel) and exactness is checked levelwise, so the category
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ of simplicial sheaves is abelian; under AC it
carries explicit coinduced injective resolutions and a bounded derived
category, with the conventions recorded in
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], whose
bounded-below injective model uses
[[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Write
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ for that bounded derived category
([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]), with its ordinary shift
$[1]$ and cone triangles.

**Cartesian cohomology.** A complex $A$ of simplicial sheaves has **Cartesian
cohomology** if for every monotone $\alpha:[p]\to[m]$ the structure morphism
$Z_\alpha^{-1}H^j(A_p)\to H^j(A_m)$ is an isomorphism for every $j$; this is
the condition that all structure morphisms of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(A)$
are isomorphisms, in the notation of
[[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]].

**Definition.** The **equivariant constructible derived category**
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$ consisting of the complexes $A$
satisfying:

1. $A$ is bounded: the single complex $A$ has only finitely many nonzero
   cohomology simplicial sheaves $H^j(A)$, i.e. there are integers $a\le b$
   with $H^j(A)=0$ for $j<a$ and $j>b$. This is uniform cohomological
   boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category; it is not a degreewise bound
   on the components $A_p$;
2. $A$ has Cartesian cohomology; and
3. the restriction $A_0$ of $A$ to the degree-zero space $Z_0=X$ has
   cohomology sheaves that are algebraically constructible with
   finite-dimensional stalks
   ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]).

**Ext and restriction.** Morphisms in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ are morphisms in the
ambient category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet))$; they are not morphisms
in the derived category of naive $G$-equivariant sheaves. Set
$\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary
cochain shift. Evaluation at $p=0$ is exact because kernels, cokernels and
cohomology of complexes of simplicial sheaves are formed levelwise, so it
induces the **forgetful functor** (restriction to $X$)
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, $A\mapsto A_0$; its target is
the bounded constructible category $D_c^b(X;k)$ of
[[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]].

**Well-formedness.** This definition fixes only the ambient category, the
object class and the conventions; the statements that make it usable — that
$D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a locally small triangulated category, that restriction to
$X$ is conservative, that coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived
morphism groups, and that the finite general linear Stiefel resolutions realize
it inside the bounded resolution triples on $X_N$ — are the content of
[[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]],
which is recorded in `justified_by` rather than in `deps` because that lemma
depends on this definition. AC is inherited from the two construction
suppliers named above and is used there for injective replacements; no further
choice principle is introduced here, and the shift convention is the ordinary
one of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, i.e. a classical
algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), regarded as
a topological space with its analytic topology
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]), and
let $k$ be a field. Write $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]],
[[def-presheaf-of-groups-rings-modules]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is
an abelian category ([[thm-abelian-sheaves-form-abelian-category]]), so its
bounded derived category $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is defined with the
conventions of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]], under the
standing smallness hypothesis recorded there.

The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ consisting of the complexes $A$ satisfying:

1. $A$ is **cohomologically bounded**: $H^j(A)=0$ for $|j|$ sufficiently large;
   and
2. $A$ is **algebraically constructible**: there exists a finite smooth
   algebraic stratification with the frontier condition $\mathfrak S$ of $X$
   ([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]) such
   that for every stratum $S\in\mathfrak S$ and every integer $j$ the
   restriction $H^j(A)|_S$ is locally constant of finite rank
   ([[def-locally-constant-sheaf-of-finite-rank]]).

These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent
sheaves. We use the shift convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]: $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$. A
groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through
an explicit local comparison, which is not made here.

Constructibility is a condition on the cohomology sheaves of a complex, and it
is quantified existentially over finite smooth algebraic frontier
stratifications: no stratification is fixed, and no existence or
common-refinement theorem for stratifications is asserted by this definition.
Shifting replaces $H^j$ by $H^{j+m}$, which preserves cohomological boundedness
and shifts a witnessing stratification nowhere, so the class is closed under
shifts and under isomorphisms in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. No choice
principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a topological
space and let $k$ be a field. The category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ of sheaves
of $k$-vector spaces is the category of modules over the ringed space
$(X,k_X)$ with constant structure sheaf $k_X$
([[def-locally-ringed-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]); it is a locally
small Grothendieck category and carries a functorial injective embedding, and
iterating that embedding on cokernels yields for every $k$-sheaf one specific
injective resolution
([[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]). These resolutions are
bounded-below injective replacements, so with the dependent choice supplied by
AC ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) the bounded-below
injective complexes model the bounded derived category:
$K^+(\operatorname{Inj}\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))\to
D^+(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ is an equivalence, and morphisms of the bounded
derived category are computed by these replacements
([[thm-injective-complexes-model-the-bounded-below-derived-category]]).

Now let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety and let
$\mathfrak S$ be a finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier
condition of $X$
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Let
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ be the full subcategory of
$D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are bounded
and constructible with respect to $\mathfrak S$
([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Then
$D^b_{\mathfrak S}(X;k)$ is a triangulated subcategory: it is closed under
shifts, isomorphisms and mapping cones. More generally, if two bounded
algebraically constructible complexes are constructible with respect to one
common finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification, then their cone is
bounded and constructible with respect to that stratification.

Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. We use cochains as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], with $X[k]^n=X^{n+k}$ and $d_{X[k]}^n=(-1)^kd_X^{n+k}$. Thus $H^n(X[k])=H^{n+k}(X)$. The cochain category $K(\mathcal A)$ is the reindexed published homotopy category. Put

$$D(\mathcal A)=K(\mathcal A)[\mathrm{qis}^{-1}],\qquad Q:K(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow D(\mathcal A).$$

Likewise $D^-,D^+,D^b$ initially mean the localizations of the termwise bounded variants of [[def-bounded-bounded-below-and-bounded-above-complex]]. Roof morphisms exist by [[lem-quasi-isomorphisms-admit-the-roof-calculus-in-the-homotopy-category]] and [[thm-the-calculus-of-fractions-constructs-the-localization]] under its standing size hypothesis: a small category of complexes, or supplied small cofinal denominator families. Every assertion of Hom sets is under that hypothesis. In the bounded module models, supplied replacements will separately exhibit those Hom sets. No general local-smallness theorem for unbounded $D(\mathcal A)$ is asserted.

The cone convention is $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, $d(y,x)=(d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$, and its triangle ends in $X[1]$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a

derivations.claim: **The ambient category and its Hom groups.** By [F1] the category $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ is abelian with levelwise exactness, has enough injectives under AC via the coinduced objects $N_pI$, and its bounded derived category is actual with set-sized Hom groups computed by bounded-below injective replacements. This is the ambient category of the definition, with the ordinary shift and cone triangles of [[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

**Closure under the triangulated operations.** Shifts and isomorphisms preserve Cartesian cohomology and the constructibility of the degree-zero restriction because the structure maps of a shifted or isomorphic complex are the shifts or conjugates of the original structure maps. For a cone $C(f)$ of a morphism $f:A\to B$ of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$, the structure maps of $C(f)$ are the cones of the levelwise structure maps, and exactness of simplicial inverse image identifies the structural comparison for $C(f)$ with the map of cones of the structural comparisons for $A$ and $B$. Those two comparisons are quasi-isomorphisms by Cartesianity, so their cone comparison is a quasi-isomorphism by the long exact cohomology sequences. Thus $C(f)$ has Cartesian cohomology. The degree-zero restriction $C(f)_0$ is the cone of $f_0$ between constructible complexes, and by the common-stratification closure of [F2] it is again constructible. Hence $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of the ambient bounded derived category.

**Conservative restriction.** Let $A\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with $A_0\cong0$ in $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$. All cohomology sheaves of $A_0$ vanish, and by Cartesianity the structure morphism of $H^j(A)$ along the projection $d_0^p:Z_p\to Z_0=X$ identifies $H^j(A)_p$ with the pullback of $H^j(A_0)$ for every $p$, so every cohomology simplicial sheaf of $A$ vanishes. An object of the bounded derived category with vanishing cohomology objects is zero by [F2], so $A\cong0$. Restriction to $X$ is thus conservative.

**The finite resolution triples.** Apply [F3] to the frame resolution of $G$: the simplicial map $p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$ is levelwise a locally trivial bundle with $r_N$-acyclic fiber, its induced pullback is compatible with the simplicial structure, and the locally split Čech descent of [F1] for the principal bundle $P_N\to X_N$ identifies the Cartesian-cohomology derived category of the nerve of $P_N$ with $D_c^b(X_N;k)$. Composing with $Q_N$ gives the identification of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory of $D_c^{[b,a]}(X_N;k)$ in the stated range: an equivariant object $A$ corresponds to the triple $(Q_N(A),\ p_N^*A\cong q_N^*Q_N(A))$, and conversely a triple whose frame pullback comes from $X$ arises from an equivariant object. The bounded Hom comparison of [F3] is induced by pullback along $p_N$ and the descent equivalence, hence carries composition to composition; at $m=0$ it is a ring comparison $\operatorname{End}_G(K)\cong\operatorname{End}_{X_N}(Q_NK)$ for objects in the interval, and retract closure is inherited from [F3].

**Idempotent completeness.** Let $e:K\to K$ be an idempotent endomorphism of a bounded object $K\in D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. Form the telescope in the bounded-below derived category of all simplicial sheaves: let $S=\bigoplus_{j\ge0}K$ be the countable sum with the shift map $1-\operatorname{shift}(e):S\to S$ sending the $j$-th summand to the $j$-th summand by $\mathrm{id}$ and to the $(j+1)$-st by $-e$, and let $T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-\operatorname{shift}(e))$. Countable coproducts in $\operatorname{Sh}_k(Z_\bullet)$ exist levelwise and are exact, and the cone is levelwise, so $H^j(T)=\operatorname{colim}_j\bigl(H^j(K)\xrightarrow{H^j(e)}H^j(K)\xrightarrow{H^j(e)}\cdots\bigr)=\operatorname{im}H^j(e)$: the colimit of an idempotent is its image, and because $H^j(e)$ is an idempotent endomorphism of the simplicial sheaf $H^j(K)$ its image is a direct summand. Thus $T$ is an object of the bounded-below ambient derived category with bounded Cartesian constructible cohomology, and by truncation it defines an object of $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. The first-summand inclusion $i:K\to T$ satisfies $ie=i$ by the telescope relations, and the map $S\to K$ with every component $e$ annihilates $1-\operatorname{shift}(e)$, so the triangle yields $p:T\to K$ with $pi=e$. Then $ip$ is an isomorphism on cohomology, hence by [F2] an isomorphism. Also $(ip)^2=i(pi)p=iep=ip$, since $ie=i$. An invertible idempotent is the identity, so $ip=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $pi=e$, splitting the idempotent inside $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$. Hence the category is idempotent complete.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1 and 2.2 give the triangulated, locally small model with conservative restriction and the finite resolution comparisons; step 2.3 gives idempotent completeness. AC is consumed exactly as recorded in [A1].
